questions.question: 78112. Which property is most important for a screening test?
questions.explain: Screening tests require high sensitivity to detect most individuals with the disease and minimize false-negative results.

questions.question: 78111. Which result meets the bacteriological standard for safe drinking water?
questions.option2: E. coli not detectable in 100 mL
questions.option4: E. coli not detectable in 1 L
questions.explain: Safe drinking water should contain no detectable E. coli in 100 mL.

questions.question: 78110. Which is the best indicator of the health status of a community?
questions.explain: Infant mortality rate (IMR) is a sensitive indicator of the overall health status and socioeconomic conditions of a community.

questions.question: 78109. Which study design is best for measuring incidence?
questions.explain: A cohort study follows disease-free individuals over time and directly measures new cases (incidence).

questions.question: 78108. What is the first-line medication and route of administration recommended for the emergency management of Anaphylaxis?
questions.explain: Prompt administration of IM Adrenaline (epinephrine) 0.3–0.5 mL of 1:1000 solution is the primary emergency management step for anaphylaxis. Antihistamines and corticosteroids serve as secondary supportive treatments.

questions.question: 78107. ​A patient presents with iron deficiency anaemia. Which of the following findings is expected on the serum iron profile?
questions.option1: Serum ferritin raised, Total iron binding capacity (TIBC) normal
questions.option2: Serum ferritin reduced, Total iron binding capacity (TIBC) raised
questions.option3: Serum ferritin normal, Total iron binding capacity (TIBC) reduced
questions.option4: Both Serum ferritin and TIBC are raised
questions.explain: In iron deficiency anaemia, the serum ferritin level decreases, reflecting depleted iron stores, while the Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC) increases.

questions.question: 78106. ​Which of the following is considered a primary triad feature of tetany due to hypocalcaemia?
questions.explain:
Triad of tetany due to hypocalcaemia

Carpopedal spasm – painful flexion of wrist and fingers

Stridor – due to laryngospasm

Convulsion – due to increased neuromuscular

questions.question: 78105. Which amino acid cannot be synthesized by the human body in sufficient amounts?
questions.explain: Histidine is an essential amino acid that must be obtained from the diet.

questions.question: 78104. Which enzyme is the rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis?
questions.explain: Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) is the major rate-limiting and regulatory enzyme of glycolysis.

questions.question: 78103. Which of the following is a stop codon?
questions.explain: UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons; AUG is the start codon.

questions.question: 78102. Radiological evidence indicating loss of anchorage during posterior tooth retraction includes:
questions.option4: Widening of PDL space on lingual aspect only
questions.explain: proclination  of the anterior/labial segment while attempting to retract posterior teeth  is a classic radiological and clinical sign of anchorage loss.

questions.question: 78101. Which of the following is a ketone body?
questions.explain: Acetoacetate is a ketone body. The other ketone bodies are β-hydroxybutyrate and acetone.

questions.question: 78100. ​Anterior bite plates increase anchorage value in fixed/removable orthodontic appliances through which mechanism?
questions.explain: An inclined or flat anterior bite plate disoccludes the posterior teeth, thereby withdrawing the occlusal interlock and allowing controlled movement or reinforcement of anchorage

questions.question: 78099. Which vitamin is essential for glucose metabolism?
questions.explain: Thiamine (vitamin B₁) is required as a coenzyme in carbohydrate metabolism, particularly for pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

questions.question: 78098. ​Which of the following is a limitation of functional appliance therapy?
questions.option2: Requires full patient compliance and active growth
questions.option3: Cannot accelerate growth in the condylar region
questions.option4: Causes severe root resorption on all anchor teeth
questions.explain: Functional appliances are removable or fixed growth-modification devices; their success relies heavily on patient compliance and the presence of active skeletal growth. They cannot be effectively used once growth has ceased

questions.question: 78097. Which transport process shows saturation kinetics?
questions.explain: Facilitated diffusion is carrier-mediated and becomes saturated when all carriers are occupied.

questions.question: 78096. Angle's Class II, Division 2 malocclusion is characteristically associated with which type of inter-incisal angle and overbite?
questions.option1: Decreased inter-incisal angle and open bite
questions.option2: High (increased) inter-incisal angle and increased overbite
questions.option3: Normal inter-incisal angle and reverse overbite
questions.option4: Low inter-incisal angle and reduced overbite
questions.explain: Class II, Division 2 features retroclined maxillary central incisors, resulting in a high (increased) inter-incisal angle and a deep, complete overbite

questions.question: 78095. Which protein binds Ca²⁺ to initiate skeletal muscle contraction?
questions.explain: Ca²⁺ binds to troponin C, causing tropomyosin to move away from actin’s myosin-binding sites and allowing contraction.

questions.question: 78094. Removal of an equivalent tooth in the opposing arch to maintain the inter-arch relationship and buccal occlusion is termed as:
questions.explain:
Balancing extraction:

Removal of a corresponding tooth on the opposite side of the same arch to maintain arch symmetry and midline balance.

​Example:

Extraction of the lower right first premolar → extraction of the lower left first premolar.

​Compensating extraction:

Removal of a corresponding/equivalent tooth in the opposing arch to maintain the inter-arch relationship and buccal occlusion.

​Example:

Extraction of an upper first molar → extraction of the opposing lower first molar.

​-- Enforced extraction:

Extraction of a tooth that is clinically unavoidable or necessary because the tooth is severely compromised, diseased, or unsuitable for retention.

​Wilkinson extraction

A term referring to an extraction approach/pattern intended to maintain occlusal and arch relationships through planned removal of teeth. It is much less commonly used than balancing and compensating extraction

questions.question: 78093. Which of the following is considered the primary and most important indication for serial extraction?
questions.explain: Arch length deficiency as compared to tooth material is the most important indication for serial extraction.

questions.question: 78092. Which is the major intracellular buffer?
questions.explain: Phosphate is the major intracellular buffer, while bicarbonate is the principal extracellular buffer.

questions.question: 78091. In infants, defecation often follows a meal. What causes the colonic contractions in this situation?
questions.explain: The gastrocolic reflex increases colonic motility following gastric distension, promoting defecation after a meal.

questions.question: 78090. Which neurotransmitter is released by preganglionic sympathetic fibres?
questions.explain: All preganglionic autonomic fibres release acetylcholine (ACh) at the autonomic ganglion.

questions.question: 78089. Main Indication of circumcision ?
questions.explain: Circumcision is mainly indicated for religious purposes .

questions.question: 78088. Which intravenous fluid is physiologically isotonic in vivo?
questions.explain: Ringer’s lactate is physiologically isotonic in vivo, whereas dextrose solutions become effectively hypotonic after glucose metabolism.

questions.question: 78087. Which feature best distinguishes a keloid from a hypertrophic scar?
questions.explain: Keloids extend beyond the original wound margins, whereas hypertrophic scars remain confined to the wound.

questions.question: 78086. Which is the most common type of thyroid carcinoma?
questions.explain: Papillary carcinoma is the most common thyroid malignancy.

questions.question: 78085. Which finding is most specific for strangulation in intestinal obstruction?
questions.explain: Continuous severe abdominal pain suggests bowel ischaemia and strangulation, whereas uncomplicated mechanical obstruction typically causes colicky pain.

questions.question: 78084. Mixed Oxygen Venous Satuaration is increased in-
questions.explain: Only in distributive shock, cell cannot utilize oxygen properly. So rise of Mixed venous oxygen saturation

questions.question: 78083. Which formula is commonly used to calculate initial fluid requirements in major burns?
questions.explain: The Parkland formula estimates fluid requirements during the first 24 hours after a major burn. The Wallace rule of nines is used to estimate burned body surface area, not fluid requirements.

questions.question: 78082. Which feature is most characteristic of dry gangrene?
questions.explain: Dry gangrene typically produces dry, shrunken, mummified tissue with a clear line of demarcation between viable and non-viable tissue.

questions.question: 78081. Which intervention should be performed immediately in a trauma patient with a tension pneumothorax?
questions.explain: Needle thoracostomy provides immediate decompression of a tension pneumothorax, followed by tube thoracostomy as definitive treatment.

questions.question: 78080. Which is the most common type of hernia to undergo strangulation?
questions.explain: Femoral hernias have a narrow, rigid neck and are therefore particularly prone to strangulation.

questions.question: 78079. Which is the most common cause of chronic pancreatitis?
questions.explain: Chronic alcohol consumption is the most common cause of chronic pancreatitis.

questions.question: 78078. Which is the most common cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding in adults?
questions.explain: Diverticular disease is the most common cause of significant lower gastrointestinal bleeding in adults.

questions.question: 78077. Which is the most common cause of secondary haemorrhage after surgery?
questions.explain: Wound infection can cause secondary haemorrhage by eroding blood vessels, typically occurring several days after surgery.

questions.question: 78076. Which clinical sign is most characteristic of acute cholecystitis?
questions.explain: Murphy’s sign is classically positive in acute cholecystitis due to pain and inspiratory arrest on palpation of the right upper quadrant.

questions.question: 78075. Which nerve is most commonly injured in a fracture of the shaft of the humerus?
questions.explain: The radial nerve runs in the spiral groove of the humerus and is particularly vulnerable in fractures of the shaft.

questions.question: 78074. Which finding is most suggestive of acute compartment syndrome after a limb fracture?
questions.explain: Pain on passive stretching is an early and characteristic clinical feature of acute compartment syndrome.

questions.question: 78073. Which is the earliest clinical sign of hypovolaemic shock?
questions.explain: Tachycardia is an early compensatory response to hypovolaemia.

questions.question: 78072. Which fetal presentation is most strongly associated with cord prolapse?
questions.explain: Breech presentation is associated with an increased risk of umbilical cord prolapse, particularly with incomplete or footling breech.

questions.question: 78071. Which organism is the causative agent of moniliasis?
questions.explain: Moniliasis is the historical term for candidiasis, most commonly caused by Candida albicans.

questions.question: 78070. Which is the most common presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma?
questions.explain: Postmenopausal bleeding is the most common presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma and should always be investigated to exclude malignancy.

questions.question: 78069. Which ovarian tumour is most commonly associated with ovarian torsion?
questions.explain: Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is a common benign ovarian tumour associated with adnexal torsion, particularly because of its relatively mobile, often solid–cystic nature.

questions.question: 78068. Which type of epithelium lines the mucosa of the gallbladder?
questions.explain: The gallbladder mucosa is lined by simple columnar epithelium with microvilli, specialized for absorption of water and electrolytes.

questions.question: 78067. Which nerve injury causes loss of sensation over the first dorsal web space?
questions.explain: The superficial radial nerve supplies sensation over the first dorsal web space.

questions.question: 78066. Which structure passes through the inguinal canal in females?
questions.explain: The round ligament of the uterus passes through the inguinal canal and terminates in the labia majora.

questions.question: 78065. The sinoatrial node is most commonly supplied by which coronary artery?
questions.explain: The SA node is supplied by the right coronary artery (RCA) in about 60% of people and by the left circumflex artery in about 40%.

questions.question: 78064. Which of the following is not an apical cell-surface specialization?
questions.explain: Microvilli, cilia and stereocilia are apical cell-surface specializations. Villi are multicellular mucosal projections containing connective tissue and blood vessels.

questions.question: 78063. A full-term newborn undergoes which sudden circulatory change at birth?
questions.explain: Lung expansion suddenly reduces pulmonary vascular resistance, increasing pulmonary blood flow after birth.
